 Portless is a tech-enabled supply chain business that helps DTC brands ship directly from Asia to customers worldwide in 5-9 days. We're transforming how ecommerce brands think about fulfillment by eliminating the traditional 60-90 day ocean freight model and replacing it with faster, more flexible, cash-flow friendly logistics.
 We're venture backed and growing fast. Our customers include brands shipping everything from apparel to consumer electronics, and we operate in 55+ countries. We're on a mission to make global fulfillment as seamless as domestic shipping.
 The Role
 We're looking for a Director of New Business Sales to lead the team of AEs responsible for winning new logos at Portless.
 You'll inherit a team of seven new business Account Executives selling into the SMB and Mid-Market segments, with ACVs most commonly associated with Enterprise deal values in other industries. These are real deals with real complexity: multiple stakeholders, operational diligence, and buyers who need to move physical product in order to go live with our solution. Your team owns those deals end-to-end, from qualified opportunity through implementation.
 This is a leadership role, not a player-coach role. You won't carry a personal quota. You will be measured on whether your team hits its number, and on whether the people on it get better while they do it. That means recruiting and retaining talent others want to hire, building a high-performance and low-ego culture, coaching at a world-class level, and knowing when to put your own hands on a deal.
 It's also a global role. Our fulfillment operations run out of Asia, and our customers are expanding into Europe, Australia, and the wider APAC region. You'll work directly with our teams on the ground in those markets and help your AEs run deal cycles across them. The time zones required to execute at a global scale demand flexibility beyond a traditional 9 to 5 and we're looking for someone who treats that as part of the opportunity rather than an inconvenience.
 What You'll Do
 Recruit and retain outstanding sales talent. You'll own hiring for the new business team as we scale beyond seven AEs, build a bench before you need it, and keep your best people here and growing.
 Build a high-performance, low-ego culture where the team makes commitments, meets them, and holds each other to a standard which demands we all do the best work of our careers. You'll set the bar for what "on track" looks like and make missing it uncomfortable without making it personal.
 Coach at a world-class level through call reviews, deal reviews, and 1:1s. You'll use our "One Thing" coaching philosophy to give each AE focused, specific feedback that measurably improves their craft.
 Get into the deals that matter. You'll bring real deal sense to your team's highest-potential opportunities, joining calls, shaping strategy, engaging senior stakeholders, and helping close business without taking the deal away from the rep.
 Own the number. You'll forecast accurately, track leading indicators, and diagnose pipeline problems early enough to do something about them.
 Run deal cycles across regions. You'll partner directly with our team in Asia and support your AEs on opportunities in Europe, Australia, and APAC.
 Develop the playbook for how new business is won at Portless, refining discovery, business case development, and competitive positioning as we scale.
 Partner cross-functionally with BDRs on target account strategy and handoff quality, with Marketing on messaging, with Onboarding and Client Success on customer transitions, and with RevOps on the systems that make the team faster.
 Maintain CRM discipline across the team, with accurate forecasting, clean deal stages, and activity logging in HubSpot.
 What We're Looking For
 Must-haves:
 3+ years of sales leadership experience managing quota-carrying Account Executives.
 Your own track record as a quota-bearing closer in the mid-market and/or enterprise space.
 Demonstrated ability to recruit great sales talent and retain it.
 Demonstrated ability to build a team culture that consistently hits its commitments.
 Demonstrated coaching ability, with specific examples of reps who measurably improved under you.
 A track record of winning deals yourself, and of helping your team win deals you were involved in.
 Comfort working across time zones, including direct collaboration with our team in Asia and deal cycles in Europe, Australia, and APAC.
 Experience with CRM and sales tools (HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, etc.).
 Nice-to-haves:
 Experience selling to ecommerce, DTC, or retail brands.
 Familiarity with logistics, supply chain, 3PL, or fulfillment industry.
 Experience with usage-based pricing models.
 Experience scaling a sales team through a period of rapid headcount growth.
 Previous experience at a high-growth startup where you helped build the sales motion.

 Coachable: You actively seek feedback and apply it fast.
 Capable: Leadership is a craft to be mastered, you care about doing so.
 Curious: When in doubt, figure it out. You are always looking to better understand your prospects, sales as a craft, and the ecommerce industry.
 Resilient: You navigate complex deals and setbacks without losing momentum.
 Driven: You're motivated by achievement and like to compete.
 Low-Ego: If you aren't a team player you will fail here.
 Why Portless

 Competitive compensation
 Equity
 Full benefits

The Toronto Star is seeking a skilled and driven journalist to join its Business and Housing team, covering the housing beat. Housing is one of the most urgent and consequential stories in Canada right now — touching affordability, development, tenant rights, municipal policy and the everyday lives of millions of Ontarians — and this reporter will be at the centre of it.
 The successful candidate will cover housing in all its dimensions: the politics of zoning and intensification, the struggles of renters and first-time buyers, the decisions of developers and city planners, the impact of interest rates and immigration on supply and demand, and the human stories behind the numbers. They will work closely with colleagues on the Business and Housing team and across the newsroom to produce journalism that is agenda-setting, accurate and deeply connected to the lives of Star readers in the GTA and beyond.
 This role sits within the Journalist classification in the Star's Editorial Department. While the initial assignment is to the housing beat within the Business and Housing team, journalists may be assigned across a variety of newsroom roles in the future. The position reports to the Senior Editor, Business and Housing.
 What you will do 
 Break and develop housing news across a broad range of topics — affordability, development, tenant rights, municipal policy, the rental market, real estate trends and the intersection of housing with broader economic and social issues.
 Generate original story ideas rooted in strong sourcing, data literacy and a genuine understanding of how housing issues affect real people across the GTA and Ontario.
 Build and maintain a deep network of sources — including city planners, developers, tenant advocates, municipal politicians, real estate economists, renters, buyers and industry insiders.
 Work collaboratively with colleagues on the Business and Housing team, as well as the visuals, multimedia and audience teams, to produce ambitious multi-platform storytelling.
 Produce a mix of daily news and longer-form enterprise and feature work, with strong written copy delivered accurately on deadline.
 Think beyond text — contributing ideas and content for video, audio and digital formats in collaboration with multimedia colleagues.
 Use data, public records and access-to-information requests to deepen and differentiate reporting.
 Maintain the Toronto Star's rigorous journalistic standards in all coverage.
Proven experience as a journalist at a daily news organization, with a track record of strong, original reporting.
 Demonstrated knowledge of or experience covering housing, real estate, urban affairs, municipal politics or related beats — or a clear and compelling case for how your reporting experience translates.
 Exceptional news judgment, writing skills and the ability to tell complex stories in ways that are clear, compelling and relevant to a broad readership.
 Strong source-building skills and the ability to work contacts across government, industry, advocacy groups and affected communities.
 Experience with data journalism, public records research and access-to-information requests — or a willingness to develop these skills.
 The ability to generate a steady stream of original, ambitious story ideas and see them through from pitch to publication.
 A self-starter mentality — able to manage multiple stories simultaneously, work independently and meet deadlines in a fast-paced newsroom.
 Comfort with digital storytelling and an understanding of how audiences consume journalism across platforms.
 Familiarity with CP style and a commitment to accuracy and fairness.
 A deep understanding of the GTA, its communities and the issues that matter most to people who live and work here.
 A demonstrated commitment to the Torstar values of collaboration, focus, selflessness, agility and results.

WANTED: One Hungry Closer Who's Sick Of Selling Other People's Dreams. 
 (Read this whole thing. If you quit halfway, we already have your answer.) 
 Most job ads read like they were written by HR. 
Bullet points. Buzzwords. 
A "competitive compensation package" that translates to "we'll pay you just enough to keep you from leaving, but never enough to actually win." 
 This isn't that.
 This is a letter. From us to you. About one of the most lopsided opportunities we've ever put in front of a salesperson and the rare, specific human being we're trying to find to fill it.
 If that human is you, you're going to feel it in your chest somewhere around paragraph nine.
 First — Who We Are. And Why It Matters. 
 We're Wealth Without Wall Street. 
 Russ Morgan and Joey Muré built this from scratch, not in a Manhattan glass tower, not with a hedge-fund pedigree, but by getting fed up watching hardworking business owners hand their financial futures to suit-wearing strangers who couldn't pick them out of a lineup.
 Together we've helped thousands of business owners, real estate investors, doctors, and high-earning professionals do what 99% of America has been brainwashed into believing is impossible:
 Generate passive income that exceeds their monthly expenses. 
 That's the whole game. That's what freedom actually looks like — not a 401(k) you can't touch until you're 65 and your knees are gone, but real cash flowing in every single month whether you work or not.
 We do it using the Infinite Banking Concept — the same wealth strategy quietly used by the richest families in America for over a century. We teach people to become their own bank. To recycle their capital. To stop renting money from institutions that profit off their ignorance.
 Russ and Joey have done it themselves. Over $50,000 per month in passive income. Co-authors of an Amazon bestseller. Hosts of one of the most respected podcasts in personal finance.
 This isn't theory. This is the real thing.
 Right now, we have more qualified people waving their hands than we can possibly talk to.
 That's where you come in.
 The Role: Business Developer. (Translation: The Person Who Decides Who Gets Free.) 
 Let us describe a typical day so you know exactly what you're signing up for.
 You wake up. You check your calendar. There are real, pre-qualified humans on it, people who registered for our workshops, devoured Russ and Joey's content, raised their hand, and said "I want a Passive Income Game Plan Session." 
 These aren't cold strangers. 
These aren't leads scraped off a list. 
These are people who already trust the brand, already believe the philosophy, and already know they're tired of the rat race.
 Your job is to pickup the phone, set appointments by making outbound calls and take inbound appointments.
Ask the kind of questions most salespeople are too soft to ask. 
Find out where they really are financially, emotionally, mentally. Diagnose whether IBC and our path is actually right for them.
 And if it is? You hand them the keys.
 You're not pitching. You're not pressuring. You're not chasing.
 You're the bridge between someone's current life — exhausted, overworked, financially fragile — and the version of their life where they sleep through the night because money is finally working for them instead of against them.
 That's the job.
 If that sounds like too much responsibility, the back button is right there.
 Who We Are NOT Looking For. 
 Let's save us both some time.
 We are not looking for the guy who calls himself a "closer" because he sold timeshares in Cabo for six months.
 We are not looking for the person who needs a six-week ramp, a personal coach, three resource Slack channels, and a "psychologically safe" environment to dial a phone.
 We are not looking for someone who's going to ghost on Friday afternoons because the surf is up.
 We are not looking for a salary chaser. If a guaranteed paycheck is what you're after, McDonald's is hiring. Go thrive.
 And we are definitely not looking for someone who can't speak from the heart about money, freedom, and the very real fear most Americans carry around about both. If you can't connect at the soul level, you can't sell this. Period.
 Who We ARE Looking For. 
 A killer. But a killer with a conscience.
 Someone who can sit across a Zoom screen from a stranger and — within ten minutes — have them admitting things they haven't told their spouse.
 Someone who's already a top performer somewhere else and is bored to tears selling SaaS, solar, or something else they couldn't care less about.
 Someone who reads Rich Dad Poor Dad , listens to BiggerPockets, follows Dave Ramsey just to argue with him, and already has an opinion about whole life insurance — even if that opinion needs updating.
 Someone with the spine to say "I don't think you're a fit. Here's why," and walk away from money on principle.
 Someone who treats every conversation like it's their last shot — because that's how the great ones do it.
 If you read those five paragraphs and felt seen, keep going.
 The Non-Negotiables.
 Proven sales background. Minimum 2+ years closing in a high-ticket, phone/Zoom-based environment. We don't care about your resume — we care about your numbers.
 25%+ close rate after probation. Below that, you're not the right fit and we'll part as friends.
 Full ownership of your pipeline. Nobody is going to chase you to follow up. The leads are there. The CRM is built. The systems work. You just have to work them. 
 Show up sharp every single day. This is a high-tempo environment. We move. We measure. We adjust.
 Live the message. If you don't believe building wealth outside the traditional system is possible, you cannot sell it. Period. Bonus points if you already own a whole life policy, have read Becoming Your Own Banker by Nelson Nash, or have personal experience with real estate investing or passive income.
 Stable, professional remote setup. High-speed internet, quiet environment, quality camera and mic. We're representing a premium brand on every single call.
 CRM discipline. You log notes the same day. You update statuses in real time. If "I forgot to update the CRM" is a phrase that comes out of your mouth more than twice, this won't work.
 Emotional intelligence over scripts. We'll give you frameworks. We will not give you a robot script to memorize. If you can't read a human, you can't sell here.
 Coachable ego. Strong opinions, loosely held. We promote killers who listen. We fire prima donnas who don't.
 A worldview that aligns. You believe people are responsible for their own freedom. You believe Wall Street is not the answer for most families. You believe in earning the right to be paid well — not waiting to be handed it.
 The Catch: 
 We get a lot of applications. 
Most won't make it past the first filter. 
We're not looking for a resume, we're looking for evidence. 
 A sales background that proves you can sit in the fire without flinching, a track record that doesn't need to be inflated, and a worldview that aligns with what we actually believe about money, freedom, and the responsibility of helping someone change their life.
 If that's you, apply. Right now. While you're feeling it.
 The Compensation. (Read This Slowly.) 
 We're going to lay this out plainly because we want you to do the math before you apply, not after.
 100% commission. Uncapped. No ceiling. No politics. 
 10% of cash collected on all Passive Income Lab Sales ($7,500 Price Point)
 20% of cash collected on all PIOS Sales ($1,000 Price Point)
 OTE for the people who actually do the work: $120K–$200K+ annually
 The top performers here aren't just closers. 
They're portfolio builders. 
Every month you close, you're stacking another stream of recurring income on top of what you closed last month. 
Twelve months in, you've got a book of business that pays you whether you take the call or not.
 Sound familiar?
 That's right. 
We pay you the same way we teach our clients to live. 
Passive income. Compounding. Freedom.
 If we wouldn't drink our own Kool-Aid with the people who sell our offer, we'd have no business selling it to anyone.
 What's In It For The Right Person. 
 Beyond the money?
 Mission that matters. You'll be the first conversation thousands of families ever have about real financial freedom. You'll be the one who makes them realize they've been lied to for thirty years, and you'll be the one who shows them the way out.
 Direct access to Russ Morgan and Joey Muré, two of the most generous, mission-driven, real-deal humans in this industry.
 Elite-level sales coaching from closers who've done eight figures in this exact niche.
 100% remote. From your kitchen. From Bali. From a coffee shop in Medellín. We don't care where the work happens. We care that the work happens.
 Pre-qualified, warm inbound leads — not cold lists, not scraped data, not random dials.
 A real product you can be proud of. No bait-and-switch. No fake scarcity. No "course that goes nowhere." A genuine pathway to freedom backed by a decade of results.

Who we are 
 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 
 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. 
 About the role: 
 Samsara is the industry leader in AI for physical operations. 
 We're hiring a Lead Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to serve as the technical anchor for ML infrastructure across Samsara's Safety AI organization. You will own the architecture and evolution of our end-to-end ML platform — spanning training, experimentation, inference, and edge deployment across more than 2M deployed devices — and be the connective tissue between applied ML teams, security, and data platform. This role is not an execution role sitting under a technical lead; you are the technical lead. Your decisions shape platform direction, unblock multiple product teams, and translate directly into real-world safety outcomes for the industries that run our world. 
 We are open to calibrating this role at Staff, Senior Staff, or Principal level depending on the candidate's scope of experience — what matters most is end-to-end platform ownership and the ability to operate as the technical anchor for the organization. 
 This is a remote position open to candidates based in the United States. 
 You should apply if: 
 You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. 
 You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go. 
 You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes. 
 You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win—together. 
 In this role, you will: 
 ML Platform & Infrastructure 
 Set the technical strategy and own end-to-end delivery of Samsara's ML platform (training, experimentation, batch/online inference, edge) — making architectural decisions and being the accountability point across all platform layers for multiple Safety AI product teams. 
 Experimentation & Measurement 
 Drive the design, launch, and iteration of Safety AI features (CV models, EcoDriving insights, LLM-based reporting) — not just enabling others to ship, but co-owning outcomes including safety metrics, reliability, and cost at production scale. 
 Inference & Edge Deployment 
 Design and operate scalable online and batch inference systems (Ray, Spark), including deployment patterns, observability, SLOs, and unified training-to-production workflows. 
 Partner with firmware and edge teams to package, validate, and deploy models to Samsara devices , and build feedback loops from edge to cloud for continuous improvement. 
 Reliability, Security & Operations 
 Own reliability, observability, and security for ML systems across cloud and edge, including on-call practices, incident response, and infrastructure hardening. 
 Own or co-own end-to-end technical delivery for high-priority or high-risk initiatives, from modeling and system design through production rollout. 
 Leadership & Culture 
 Be the technical authority for ML infrastructure architecture across Safety AI — setting direction that cross-functional teams (applied ML, firmware, security, data platform) execute against, mentoring senior engineers and applied scientists, and ensuring platform decisions are made at the right level of abstraction with the right trade-offs. 
 Drive strong developer experience through documentation and best practices, while contributing to and representing Samsara in open source communities (Ray, Spark, RayDP). 
 Champion and role model Samsara’s cultural principles: Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team . 
 Minimum requirements for the role: 
 10+ years in machine learning engineering, with demonstrated tech lead ownership of at least two major ML platform domains (distributed training, data/research infrastructure, cloud inference, or feature engineering) serving multiple product teams at scale. 
 Proven record of shipping ML-powered features end-to-end — from design through production and iteration — with measurable impact on product or business metrics (not just building internal tooling). 
 Hands-on Ray and Kubernetes expertise in production environments; Spark experience strongly preferred. Able to be a credible peer to the most senior engineers on the team. 
 Deep understanding of ML fundamentals beyond pipelines: evaluation methodology, dataset design, ablation, drift, and the ability to review and redirect modeling approaches — you bridge research and engineering, not just serve them. 
 Demonstrated cross-org technical leadership around platform decisions, and influencing roadmap and go/no-go calls based on throughput, latency, and cost trade-offs. 
 Experience navigating science-engineering tension — knowing when to hold the platform line and when to adapt for research velocity, and communicating that clearly to both sides. 
 An ideal candidate also has: 
 Prior contributions to open source projects (Ray, Spark, RayDP, or Kubernetes). 
 Experience with enterprise security/compliance in ML environments. 
 Background working with edge/on-device ML and firmware/embedded teams.

MID-MARKET IMPLEMENTATION SPECIALIST

Hi! I'm Daryl, and I'm the Manager of High Touch (Mid-Market) Implementations at Ashby. One of my favorite things about this team is that we're the first real proof point for a new customer; from day 1, we get the hands-on opportunity to show them why they made the right call switching to Ashby.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we added more than 2,100 new customers in the last year alone and now support over 5,000 customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. We're expecting similarly fast growth this year, and every one of those new customers needs a thoughtful implementation to actually get value out of Ashby. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're expanding this team!




THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Mid-Market Implementation Specialist who excels at leading technically complex, hands on implementation projects for B2B SaaS customers. You'll own each implementation from the moment Sales hands it off through go-live; part project manager, part technical expert, and part trusted advisor to the customer!

Six months in, success looks like carrying a full book of 15-20 active implementations, running each customer relationship on your own (kickoff, timeline, follow-through), independently solving complex configuration and workflow challenges, and handling the normal bumps (a slow-to-respond customer, a technical snag, an escalation) without the rest of your book slipping. It also means you're starting to make things better beyond your own accounts: you've found at least one process or documentation gap and fixed it, and you're feeding real customer feedback back to our Product team.




YOU WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY:

 - Managing 15-20 active mid-market implementations at a time (8-10 weeks implementation timeline on average), building each customer's project plan from handoff through go-live, and staying on top of timelines, hurdles, and follow-up along the way

 - Getting genuinely comfortable with the in’s and out’s of how our products work, so you can troubleshoot and advise instead of just walking through a checklist

 - Advising on what’s worked well for similar customers in the past, challenging assumptions when appropriate, and recommending configurations and workflows that balance customer needs with implementation best practices

 - Partnering closely with cross-functional partners across the business, especially Sales and CS to ensure a seamless customer journey, and Product/Engineering to flag real issues and align on a path forward

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who gets energy from both sides of this: the structure of running a tight project plan, and the judgment to rethink that plan when a customer's business genuinely calls for it.



If you have the majority of the following, you could be a great fit for this role: 

 - 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing role, with the majority of your focus on leading full-cycle B2B SaaS implementations

 - Proven track record successfully managing concurrent mid-market implementation projects without compromising quality, customer experience, or timelines

 - Experience operating with real autonomy and to own the implementation project plans end-to-end

 - Comfortable getting into the weeds of complex, multi-module software, and building genuine fluency in how it all fits together

 - Resourceful when there's no documented answer; you do your own testing and discovery, then use what you learn to advise customers on best practices and recommendations

 - Data-driven and detail-oriented, with a genuine instinct for coaching customers through unfamiliar territory

If you need someone else to do any of the following, then this role is probably not for you:

 - Independently investigate complex customer questions and become the technical/product subject matter expert during implementations

 - Carry more than a handful of accounts at once (this is a high volume role on a team that moves with urgency)

 - Own the execution of a project plan, not just its design

 - Iterate and improve on existing processes




INSTRUCTIONS

Please take your time with your application and the application questions. Although we use AI to assist in our review, we never use AI to auto-qualify or disqualify candidates. We lay eyes on each and every application, and speak to a very select number of candidates based on the application as a whole. This is an evergreen opening, so there is no need to rush, and there are no prizes for being first!




OUR PHILOSOPHY

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

 - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

 - We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles to get a sense of what we are looking for in folks on the team.




THE INTERVIEW

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

 - 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

 - 45 min - Interview with Manager of High Touch Implementations

 - 60 min- Mock Call with an Implementation Specialist and Customer Success Manager

 - Final Round:
   
   - 30 min - Cross-Functional Interview with Head of Professional Services
   
   - 30 min - Product Complexity Interview with VP of Customer Success
   
   - 30 min - Customer Adoption & Enablement with Manager of High Touch Customer Success and a High Touch Customer Success Manager
   
   - 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager




BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - You get to sell a product that our prospects & customers are truly excited about.

 - Competitive compensation is offered.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval

Jobber helps small home service businesses - plumbers, electricians, painters, landscapers - quote, schedule, invoice and get paid, while giving their customers an easy and professional experience. Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work and Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, Automations Platform to be part of our AI Workflows product organization.



The team:

The Automations Platform team builds the system that lets Jobber Teammate, our AI teammate for home service businesses, do a service provider's work for them. Every automation in Jobber runs on what this team builds.



The role:

You'll make it possible for Jobber Teammate to automate every task in Jobber.

Today a handful of automations exist and each one is expensive to build. The ambition is that every task a service provider repeats in their week has an automation that does it for them. Getting there takes two things at once, and this role does both.

You'll build the platform: the authoring, execution and evaluation models that let any product team at Jobber ship an automation without first becoming AI specialists. Skill files, tool calls, and evals that make an automation measurably better over time.

You'll also build on the platform: choosing the automations that matter most, shipping them yourself, and making them easy to find, enable and trust. Being the platform's hardest customer is what keeps it honest.

Over time you'll open it up, so service providers create their own and the best ones spread to businesses like theirs.

This suits someone equally at home in an architecture discussion and a customer interview.



As Senior Product Manager you will:

 - Build a deep understanding of home service businesses and the repeated work that consumes their week.

 - Own the automation platform: how automations are authored, how they execute, and how they're evaluated and improved.

 - Make it fast and cheap for any Jobber team to ship an automation, and measure yourself on their throughput rather than your own.

 - Build the highest-impact automations yourself, and make them easy for service providers to find, enable and trust.

 - Build an Evals platform, that makes it easy to iterate on and improve automations so the quality bar is constantly raising

 - Bring the product requirements to our AI Foundations engineering team, who build the underlying agent infrastructure.

 - Define the metrics that tell you the platform works: cost and speed of building an automation, engagement with the ones we ship, and growth of the library.



To be successful, you should have:

 - 5+ years of product management experience, with evidence of shipping real AI products and seeing them through to long-term outcomes.

 - A growth mindset and someone who thrives in change and ambiguity. The AI Org you’ll join is a fast moving space and we expect that the technology, positioning, scope and roles will all continue to evolve as we learn together

 - Experience building an AI platform was genuinely adopted - won through advocacy, tooling, and documentation.

 - Experience shipping LLM-backed or ML-backed products, with real respect for how they fail.

 - A track record of making a contested technical decision and making it stick.

 - Comfort thinking in unit economics, because the cost of building an automation decides whether this strategy is real.



Bonus points if you have:

 - Experience with agent frameworks, tool calling, or evaluation and observability systems for AI.

 - Experience with workflow automation, or no-code and low-code builder products.

 - Experience in home services, field service, or SMB software.



Hiring Process:

 - An interview with a Talent team member (45 mins)

 - A Hiring Manager Interview (60 mins)

 -  A take-home challenge with a follow-up Functional Interview (90 mins)

 - A Senior Leadership Interview (30 mins)

 

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person. This role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Toronto, Edmonton, Vancouver, and Boston.


Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $125,800, a midpoint of $147,900, and a maximum salary of $170,100, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth. 

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development. We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

 Concevoir des expériences entre les différentes fonctions afin d’accélérer le perfectionnement des bassins de talents ciblés et de gérer des projets spéciaux liés aux talents

Fidus is a global high-tech design firm headquartered in Ottawa, with additional design centres in Kitchener-Waterloo and San Jose. We specialize in leading-edge electronic product development, with hardware, embedded software, FPGA/ASIC, and signal integrity teams working together to design and deliver next-generation products for clients in emerging technology markets.
 Position Overview/Mandate: 
 The Senior Embedded Software Designer plays a key role in designing and delivering complex embedded software systems for Fidus clients. You will lead and contribute to embedded software development across communication, networking, and video applications—developing BSP-level software, implementing device drivers, integrating with FPGA SoCs and hardware, and setting technical direction for project teams.
 This role is ideal for someone with deep embedded expertise who enjoys working with new technologies, takes pride in producing maintainable, high-quality code, and is ready to provide technical leadership and mentorship while working closely with customers.
 Make an Impact with US: 
 At Fidus, you'll work on high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems, often using emerging technologies before they reach the broader market. You'll collaborate across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design as part of cross-functional teams delivering real products for our clients.
 In practice, that means contributing to projects across Communications, Aerospace & Defence, Life Sciences and Medical Devices, Space and Satellite, Industrial Automation, Automotive, and Semiconductor engagements. You won't be limited to a single product or industry—your work will follow the technology, not just one roadmap.
 What You'll Be Doing: 
 Lead and contribute to embedded software development projects, focusing on communication, networking, and video applications.
 Develop and maintain BSP-level software for embedded Linux, RTOS, and bare-metal systems.
 Implement device drivers, manage kernel configurations, and utilize build systems such as Yocto or PetaLinux.
 Design and debug software for FPGA SoCs, integrating with hardware and other system components.
 Collaborate on HW/SW/FPGA integration, interpreting schematics and datasheets to ensure robust system functionality.
 Utilize tools like oscilloscopes and logic analyzers for effective debugging and optimization.
 Define architecture and set technical direction for projects.
 Lead project teams, mentoring and guiding multiple designers to ensure high-quality outcomes.
 Work closely with customers to understand requirements and exceed expectations.
 Employ best design practices to produce maintainable and high-quality code.
 Stay current with emerging technologies and methodologies, bringing innovative solutions to the team and projects.
 Who You are: 
 Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.
 Minimum 8 years' experience in BSP-level software development within embedded Linux, RTOS, or bare-metal environments.
 Minimum 2 years' experience as a technical lead, with proven leadership in project teams, technical architecture, and direction-setting.
 Expertise in embedded software design, including communication, networking, and video applications.
 Strong experience with embedded Linux, including Yocto or PetaLinux flows, build systems, packaging, kernel configurations, and device drivers.
 Practical experience with FPGA SoCs, especially Xilinx or equivalent.
 Proficiency in C, C++, and assembly programming, with an understanding of tools and best practices for embedded environments.
 Familiarity with device driver development for Linux and real-time OSes.
 Experience with software upgrade processes and bootloaders like u-boot.
 Skills in HW/SW/FPGA integration and debugging using schematics, datasheets, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.
 Strength in object-oriented design principles and implementation.
 Knowledge of scripting languages such as Python, Bash, and TCL.
 Embraces AI as part of a modern engineering toolkit.
 Excellent communication skills, fluency in English, and ability to work effectively in a team and with clients.
 Strong technical leadership, emphasizing quality design practices.
 Willingness to learn new technologies and tackle complex challenges.
 Location and travel: Position is based in Canada. Travel may be required domestically and internationally to support customer engagements and project delivery.
 This position may require access to export-controlled information. Candidates will be required to complete background checks and security screening under Canada's Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and may also be required to obtain a security clearance under the Contract Security Program (CSP) administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC, formerly PWGSC).
 This role is an evergreen position.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted.  - Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of most roles. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events. 


How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

💖 Company-wide wellness days (1 per quarter)
